name: Towel Grip Pull-Up
description: The towel grip pull-up drapes one or two towels over a pull-up bar and has the lifter grip the hanging ends rather than the bar itself. The unstable, thick towel grip dramatically increases forearm and grip strength demands compared to standard pull-ups. This variation is used to develop crushing grip strength and is a popular training tool for climbers and grapplers.

execution.starting_position: Drape one or two towels over a pull-up bar. Grip the hanging ends of the towels with both hands. Hang at full arm extension.
execution.setup_instructions: Use gym towels or thick rope draped over a sturdy bar. Ensure the towels are secure and cannot slip off.
steps: Step 1: Grip the hanging ends of the towels with both hands, palms facing each other (neutral grip).
Step 2: Begin hanging with elbows fully extended.
Step 3: Depress and retract the scapulae, then pull the elbows down and back.
Step 4: Continue pulling until the chin clears the bar or the chest approaches the bar.
Step 5: Lower under control to full hang and repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the pull, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Letting the grip slip by not squeezing the towel tightly enough
Using momentum to compensate for grip fatigue
safety_considerations: Ensure towels are securely draped and will not slip off the bar mid-set
Grip failure can result in a sudden fall — perform over a padded surface
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full arm extension at the bottom to chin above the knot level at the top.
coaching_cues: Squeeze the towel as hard as possible throughout
Pull the elbows to your pockets
